description:
Transforms a score matrix into various kinds of normalized martices
   
   For matrices with any data type, can convert from dense to sparse, or sparse to dense, or change the datatype.

parameters.name: Dense
parameters.help: Write a dense distance matrix hdf5 file to this path.

parameters.name: Dense Text
parameters.help: Write a dense distance matrix tsv file to this path.

parameters.name: Sparse
parameters.help: Write a sparse distance matrix hdf5 file to this path.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.help: what kind of values should be in the output matrix. score: raw score, bool: 1 if a hit otherwise 0, score_dist: 1 - (score / min(row_max, col_max)), norm_score: score/min(row_max, col_max), efi_score: -log10[2^(-score) * (input_seq_length * reference_seq_length)], efi_score_dist: 1 - (efi_score / min(row_max, col_max)). Default: norm_score

advanced_parameters.name: Input Type
advanced_parameters.help: If the type of the input matrix is not specified, specify the type of input matrix. Default: None

advanced_parameters.name: Max Output Gb
advanced_parameters.help: Fail if a projected output file would exceed this many GB. Set to 0 to disable the guardrail.

advanced_parameters.name: MST
advanced_parameters.help: Keep only the edges of the maximum spanning tree (forest). The clusters are the same as the full graph's, with the connections inside each cluster pruned to the minimum needed to keep it connected. Combine with kNN to also keep each node's nearest neighbors. Uses the post-transform values; not available for distance modes.

advanced_parameters.name: kNN
advanced_parameters.help: Keep only OR-symmetric K-nearest-neighbor edges (K at least 1): an edge is kept if it is among the K best for either of its nodes. On its own this can split a cluster of the full graph into several; combine with MST to keep the clusters connected. Uses the post-transform values; not available for distance modes.
